title: Penataquit Creek (Bay Shore)
summary: Penataquit is a Bay Shore placename associated with Penataquit Creek and with older boundary language for Aweeksa Neck in Islip.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Penataquit Creek point from USGS/TopoZone feature data; not an exact crooked-tree boundary marker or historic creek-head coordinate.
introduction_content: Penataquit is connected with Bay Shore in the town of Islip and with the creek from which the former local name was taken.
history_content: Penataquit belongs to the Bay Shore creek landscape near Awixa Brook, Cagoqunk, and Orawac Brook. Boundary, spelling, and interpretation details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Related forms include Penataquitt, Penettiquott, Panothticutt, and Penatuckgut. The name may refer either to a crooked creek or to a crooked tree; the early forms favor the crooked-tree interpretation, possibly a boundary marker.

Why Place Names Matter

“When you put a name on a map or you change the name of a place, you impose your own name. That’s a way of asserting your authority over the territory.”

— Derek A. Smith, Interview in Traditional Land Use (2018), Quoted statement in article paragraph 20
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point on modern Penataquit Creek in Bay Shore. The map placement is not an exact historic boundary, creek-head, or crooked-tree location.
